Karthik —

Thanks for the proposal. Short version: the numbers are outside our budget and we have competing quotes from a vendor who can come in ~18% lower. We value Redwood's model quality but our board is pushing hard on costs this quarter.

Our three asks to stay with Redwood:
1) A short-term credit to cover the first two months (our usage spikes in Q3),
2) A firm 99.95% uptime SLA or a compensatory credit schedule in the contract,
3) A price reset if usage drops below a certain threshold mid-term (we can commit to a 6–9 month review window).

If Redwood can't provide a combination of (1) + (2) or (1) + (3) we will likely move to the lower-cost vendor. I need a definitive answer by COB 2029-05-21.

Team — escalating Pillar Health (DL-8192). Customer signaled an RFP from a lower-cost vendor and needs a definitive answer by COB 2029-05-21. Summary below and attached proposal + pricing model. 

Customer asks (they said choose any combo):
- Two-month one-time credit covering Q3 spike (approx $120k gross)
- 99.95% SLA with clear credit ladder OR a 6–9 month pricing review clause tied to usage

Background/context:
- Current ARR: $1.2M (they renew for the account at $1.8M proposed)
- Strategic: pillar_health uses Redwood for clinical search + live assist; migrating would be non-trivial; risk to retention is high if we lose search accuracy.
- Legal: wants limited contract language; Pillar Legal will push on indemnities but are open to standard addenda.

Ask from deal desk / execs: 
1) Approval for a one-time credit up to $120k (or approve range $80k–$120k),
2) Approval to add a 99.95% SLA addendum for this customer or an SLA credit schedule (finance to confirm P&L hit),
3) Permission to include an optional mid-term pricing reset clause (6 months) to avoid a full churn risk — this should be conditional on usage floor and tied to an exec-signed amendment so we can revert to list if usage recovers.

Proposed neutral position (my recommendation): Offer option B from the spreadsheet — 10% ongoing discount + 30-day SLA credit for the annual term, capped to a $95k TCV impact. If execs will not approve ongoing discount, then approve a $100k one-time credit + SLA addendum limited to 12 months.

Please advise quickly — customer deadline is next Tuesday, 2029-05-21.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / Marissa / Marcus —

Reviewed the numbers with finance and pricing ops. Quick answers: 
- One-time credit: we can approve up to $75k without Exec signoff (deal desk limit). Anything above $75k requires VP signoff (> $75k) and CFO awareness.
- SLA addendum: Legal has a standard 99.95% SLA template; we can attach it but credits beyond 30 days aggregate to a material impact — need to mark in the SOW what triggers credits. Legal wants explicit SLO measurement sources (we should call out trace IDs / infra used for measurement).
- Mid-term price reset: this is highly unusual. If we do a conditional reset clause, it needs strict triggers (usage floor X, review window Y) and a rollback mechanism. We prefer a capped one-time credit + SLA addendum over an open reset.

Recommendation from deal desk: Offer the customer a capped package: $75k one-time credit + attach 99.95% SLA addendum (12 months) with standard measurement language. If they insist on a larger concession, escalate to Marcus for final approval.

If Marcus signs off to extend to $100k, we should tie the extra $25k to a 12-month auto-renewal at agreed terms and require a purchase order on or before 2029-06-15.

Ben Carter
Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
